criteria.argument_values: A max_rows that is negative, not an integer, or too large for its successor to fit reports unsupported_value naming max_rows, and nothing launches. row_limit is reserved for a completed bounded fetch that returns more rows than allowed.
criteria.limit_unified: Defective max_rows arguments and over-full results both report row_limit carrying the supplied limit. Callers see one bound error whether the defect appears before launch or after the fetch.
criteria.review_needed: These placements cannot be separated on the supplied evidence, or neither preserves the contracts.

max_rows_errors.instructions: Decide which error covers bad max_rows arguments and which covers observed overflow. Consult common with topics.max_rows_errors.

criteria.connect_await: Opening builds the client, waits for the native connect handshake, and hands back the pool only after it succeeds. Refused and rejected connections fail open itself with connection_failed, so every returned pool has demonstrated reachability.
criteria.lazy_documented: Opening only builds the client and returns it; the first query is what discovers refusal or rejection. Documentation states plainly that a returned pool proves nothing about reachability.
criteria.probe_query: Opening runs a constant SELECT 1 through the normal query path and throws its row away, using that round trip as the reachability demonstration.
criteria.review_needed: The establishment proof cannot be decided on the supplied evidence, or no option preserves the contracts.

pool_open_proof.instructions: Decide which mechanism demonstrates that pool_open reached the server instead of deferring discovery. Consult common with topics.pool_open_proof.

criteria.propagate_fault: Classification consumes PostgresError values only. Any foreign throw from the driver continues to the generic fault machinery, keeping implementation defects distinguishable from genuine query outcomes.
criteria.query_failed_unknown: The finite mapping absorbs all native throws: anything lacking SQLSTATE and driver code becomes query_failed with code unknown. No throw from the tag call bypasses the query errors.
criteria.review_needed: Unknown-shape handling cannot be decided on the supplied evidence, or neither approach preserves the contracts.

unknown_failures.instructions: Decide where native throws outside the documented PostgresError shapes land. Consult common with topics.unknown_failures.

fixed_constraints: pool_open may emit only credentials_missing and connection_failed; every query operation may emit only its catalogue-fixed subset of unsupported_value, connection_failed, query_failed, constraint_failed, row_missing, row_count, row_limit, and schema_mismatch. Each native failure lands in one of these with scrubbed fields, never exposing messages, details, URLs, or credentials.

On Bun 1.4.2, SQL construction performs no I/O even against a dead port. The awaited connect call settles to the same client object, tolerates repetition, and raises ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_REFUSED or the server-side error when the server cannot be reached. A query issued after close raises ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED. Server failures expose a 5-character SQLSTATE through errno and usually a constraint name, while their message and detail strings may quote row values.

The top-level LIMIT travels as a bound value: 2 for one/optional results and max_rows+1 for many results. max_rows is caller-controlled integer input, so malformed bounds are visible before launch and surplus rows only after the capped fetch. Malformed parameters must block the launch entirely.

Bound descriptors contain single statements already accepted by the upstream parser, so any syntax complaint from one indicates driver malfunction, not author fault. Unexpected throws elsewhere already convert to standard failures through the shared fault path.
common.purpose: Judge only from the material given in this request. No browsing, implementation, or explanation. Where the material leaves candidates tied, select the designated uncertainty option.

max_rows_errors.facts: query_rows can raise unsupported_value keyed by path as well as row_limit keyed by limit. Negativity and successor overflow show before the native call; excess rows show after it. Neither case may quietly stretch or clip the requested bound.

pool_open_proof.facts: Lazy construction leaves a construct-only open unable to tell a live server from a dead socket, although connection_failed is still assigned to pool_open. The connect wait completes the handshake with no query payload, while a probe completes it with a wasted round trip and a discarded row.

unknown_failures.facts: All witnessed driver failures are PostgresError instances carrying code, with server failures adding errno and frequently constraint. A throw of any other shape is unwitnessed and could only come from inside the driver implementation. The mapping must remain finite in all cases.
